finding.claim: Unsigned tokens are accepted when the verifier key option is a falsy but defined value ('' or null) and algorithms are configured (e.g. ['HS256']). Signature verification is skipped entirely.
finding.source: Attacker-supplied token string with an empty signature segment: base64url(header {alg:HS256}) . base64url(claims) .
finding.sink: validateAlgorithmAndSignature skips verifySignature when signature is empty (verifier.js:169), so the payload is returned as authenticated (verifier.js:426).

trace.note: keyType check accepts typeof 'string' (including '') and 'object' (including null)
guard `if (key && keyType !== 'function')` is false, so key is never prepared and the empty-key check in prepareKeyOrSecret (verifier.js:38-40) is never reached
allowedAlgorithms keeps the configured list (e.g. ['HS256'])
token split on '.'; trailing '.' yields empty signatureSegment
BASE64URL_RE /^[A-Za-z0-9_-]*$/ accepts empty signature
hasKey = !!key evaluates to false
`hasKey && !signature` is false and `!hasKey && signature` is false, so neither check fires
header.alg 'HS256' is in allowedAlgorithms, check passes
`if (signature && ...)` is false, so no signature verification occurs
payload returned as valid

finding.guards_checked: Base64url alphabet regex (decoder.js:41); separator-count check (decoder.js:24); key type check (verifier.js:507); hasKey presence checks (verifier.js:274-278); allowed-algorithm list (verifier.js:162). None rejects an unsigned token when key is falsy. Signer rejects empty key (signer.js:215-218), so the gap is verifier-only. Not executed; established by reading.

finding.claim: With an HS-only algorithms list, a PEM public key passed as key is used as an HMAC secret. An attacker who has the public key can forge HS256 tokens.
finding.source: Attacker-supplied token with alg HS256; the attacker holds the public PEM, which is not secret.
finding.sink: verifySignature HS branch (crypto.js:341-345) validates the HMAC keyed with the public PEM bytes, via createSecretKey in prepareKeyOrSecret (verifier.js:42).

trace.note: detectPublicKeyAlgorithms(key, allowedAlgorithms) called with HS-only list
every allowed algorithm is HS, so PEM detection is skipped and allowed list returned
prepareKeyOrSecret(key, true) because availableAlgorithms[0] is HS
isSecret branch: createSecretKey(PEM bytes)
validateAlgorithmAndSignature runs HMAC verification with the public PEM as secret

finding.guards_checked: Upstream comment states HS-only skip is intentional (crypto.js:260-261). No refusal or warning for PEM keys under HS-only config. Precondition is developer misconfiguration. Authentication-relevant; flag for maintainer review. Not executed.

finding.claim: When caching is enabled and the token has an exp claim, maxAge is not enforced on cache hits. Tokens can be accepted for up to cacheTTL after iat+maxAge.
finding.source: Previously issued, validly signed token with iat and exp, replayed after maxAge has elapsed, after an earlier verification within the window.
finding.sink: Cache-hit return at verifier.js:377 (handleCachedResult) skips the maxAge validator (verifier.js:616-618), which only runs on a cache miss.

trace.note: cacheSet: when payload.exp is a number, cacheValue[2] = exp*1000 + clockTolerance; maxAge branch (126-127) not reached
entry capped at now + clockTolerance + cacheTTL (default 600000 ms, verifier.js:499)
cache lookup before any validation
range check uses only the cache's own min/max, not iat+maxAge
cache hit returns cached payload without running validators
maxAge validator exists only on the miss path (verifyToken at verifier.js:424)

finding.guards_checked: Cache is opt-in (createCache at verifier.js:83-86). Cache range check (verifier.js:368-375) does not reference maxAge. exp check is also skipped on hits but bounded by min(exp, now+cacheTTL). Impact bounded to roughly cacheTTL past the maxAge deadline. Not executed.

finding.claim: Claim validators for allowedAud, allowedIss, allowedSub, allowedJti, allowedNonce and maxAge are silently skipped when the claim is absent, so a validly signed token missing the claim passes.
finding.source: Validly signed token from the same key that omits aud, iss, sub, jti, nonce or iat. Issuers can produce these, e.g. via signer noTimestamp (signer.js:96), or a sibling service.
finding.sink: Audience/issuer/age check that should reject the token (verifier.js:304-322).

trace.note: validators loop over configured claim checks
`if (!(claim in payload)) continue` skips the check when the claim is absent
requiredClaims enforcement is opt-in; without it nothing rejects missing claims
noTimestamp yields iat undefined, so maxAge validator is skipped for such tokens

finding.guards_checked: requiredClaims (verifier.js:293-299) rejects missing claims but is opt-in. Signature and typ checks still run. Unlike jsonwebtoken, a missing aud is not rejected when audience is configured. Design-dependent severity: low to medium.

finding.claim: Verifying a Buffer token throws a TypeError when caching is enabled, because the default cacheKeyBuilder calls String.prototype.split on a Buffer.
finding.source: Caller passes a Buffer token (accepted by verify at verifier.js:353 and by index.d.ts:50).
finding.sink: hashToken calls token.split (utils.js:46), which does not exist on Buffer, so the verifier throws.

trace.note: Buffer tokens are accepted
cacheKeyBuilder(token) called with raw Buffer when cache is set
token.split('.', 1) on Buffer throws TypeError

finding.guards_checked: Failure is a thrown exception, so it fails closed and is not an authentication bypass. Correctness bug only.
